abstract: We propose a protocol to construct the 35 $f$-controlled phase gates of a three-qubit refined Deutsch-Jozsa (DJ) algorithm, by using single-qubit $\sigma_{z}$ gates, two-qubit controlled phase gates, and two-target-qubit controlled phase gates. Using this protocol, we discuss how to implement the three-qubit refined DJ algorithm with superconducting transmon qutrits resonantly coupled to a single cavity. Our numerical calculation shows that implementation of this quantum algorithm is feasible within the present circuit QED technique. The experimental realization of this algorithm would be an important step toward more complex quantum computation in circuit QED.

specification.problem: Construct the 35 f-controlled phase gates of a three-qubit refined Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm using single-qubit sigma_z gates, two-qubit controlled phase gates, and two-target-qubit controlled phase gates, and implement the algorithm with superconducting transmon qutrits resonantly coupled to a single cavity (circuit QED).
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the gate-decomposition protocol and the circuit-QED implementation goal; detailed pulse sequences, Hamiltonian parameters, refined-DJ definition and numerical results are not given in the abstract.

specification.initial_state: Assumed: all three qubits in |0>, then Hadamard-type preparation into uniform superposition (refined DJ details not given).

steps.description: Prepare the three qubits in an equal superposition (assumed standard DJ preparation).
Apply one of the 35 f-controlled phase gates U_f, each built from single-qubit sigma_z, two-qubit controlled-phase, and two-target controlled-phase gates.
Apply final Hadamard-type rotations (assumed) to map the constant/balanced distinction onto measurable outcomes.

specification.measurement: Assumed: projective measurement of all three qubits in the computational basis; the all-zero outcome indicates constant f and any other outcome balanced f (standard DJ; refined variant details not in abstract).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Classify f as constant if the outcome is 000, else balanced; compare outcome statistics with ideal to assess fidelity.
assumptions: Standard DJ preparation and readout used in place of unspecified refined DJ details
The refined DJ algorithm is assumed to share the standard DJ promise and all-zero readout rule
